subject: physics
title: Structure of the atom
key_idea: An atom has a tiny, positively charged **nucleus** of protons and neutrons, with negatively charged electrons around it. Almost all the mass is in the nucleus. Electrons sit at set energy levels and move when they absorb or emit electromagnetic radiation.

sections.heading: What an atom is made of

blocks.text: Every atom has a central nucleus surrounded by electrons. This section covers the three particles, their charges and masses, and why an atom has no overall charge.

items.meaning: The tiny, positively charged centre of the atom, made of protons and neutrons.
A positively charged particle in the nucleus.
A particle in the nucleus with no charge.
A negatively charged particle that orbits the nucleus.

items: The nucleus is positively charged because it holds the protons.
Almost all of the mass of an atom is in the nucleus, because electrons have a very small mass.
In an atom the number of protons equals the number of electrons.
The positive and negative charges balance, so an atom has no overall charge.
The nucleus holds the protons and neutrons and is positively charged.
Electrons are negatively charged and have a very small mass.
Protons and electrons are equal in number, so atoms are neutral.

blocks.text: Atoms are very small, and the nucleus is far smaller still. Most of an atom is empty space.

items: An atom has a radius of about 1 × 10⁻¹⁰ m. This is the typical size of atoms and small molecules.
The radius of the nucleus is less than 1/10 000 of the radius of the atom.
The nucleus has almost all of the mass, in a very small volume.

blocks.label: Ratio of atom to nucleus
blocks.formula: ratio = radius of atom ÷ radius of nucleus
where: The radii are in the same unit, for example metres (m).

blocks.text: An atom of radius 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁰ m with a nucleus of radius 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁵ m gives 10⁻¹⁰ ÷ 10⁻¹⁵ = 10⁵. The atom is 100 000 times wider than its nucleus.
Length of a line of atoms

blocks.label: Diameter
where: diameter and radius are in metres (m).

blocks.label: Length of a line of atoms
blocks.formula: length = number of atoms × diameter of one atom
where: length and diameter are in metres (m).

items: An atom has a radius of about 1 × 10⁻¹⁰ m.
The nucleus has a radius less than 1/10 000 of the atom.
Use the diameter, which is twice the radius, to find the length of a line of atoms.

blocks.text: Electrons are arranged at different distances from the nucleus. These distances are different energy levels.

items.meaning: A set distance from the nucleus at which an electron can orbit.
An electron that has absorbed energy and moved to a higher energy level.
An atom that has lost or gained electrons, so it has an overall charge.

diagram.alt: Compare an electron absorbing radiation with an electron emitting radiation.
items: Absorbs radiation
Emits radiation
An electron absorbs electromagnetic radiation to move to a higher energy level.
An electron emits electromagnetic radiation when it falls to a lower energy level.
If an outer electron absorbs enough energy it leaves the atom. This is called ionisation.
An atom that loses outer electrons becomes a positive ion.
Changes in atoms and nuclei can generate and absorb radiation over a wide frequency range. Gamma rays come from the nucleus.
Electrons move up an energy level by absorbing radiation and down by emitting it.
Losing an outer electron makes a positive ion.
The emitted or absorbed radiation can be from any part of the electromagnetic spectrum.

checks.q: Give the relative charge and position of a proton, a neutron and an electron.
checks.a: Proton: +1, in the nucleus. Neutron: 0, in the nucleus. Electron: -1, orbiting the nucleus.

checks.q: Explain why an atom has no overall charge.
checks.a: It has the same number of protons and electrons. The positive and negative charges balance.

checks.q: Describe what happens to an electron when it absorbs electromagnetic radiation, and what happens when it emits it.
checks.a: When it absorbs radiation it moves to a higher energy level, further from the nucleus. When it emits radiation it moves to a lower energy level, closer to the nucleus.

worked_example.question: Explain how an electron can move up and down between energy levels in an atom.
answer_points: To move to a higher energy level an electron absorbs energy from electromagnetic radiation.
To move to a lower energy level an electron emits energy in the form of electromagnetic radiation.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each direction. Absorbing energy by collision with another electron is also accepted for the move up.

blocks.text: A positron is a particle emitted from some nuclei. It is the positive equivalent of an electron.

rows: Very small (the same as an electron)

worked_example.question:
An atom has a central nucleus containing neutrons and protons. Electrons orbit the nucleus.
An atom has a radius of 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁰ m.
A nucleus has a radius of 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁵ m.

Calculate the ratio of the radius of the atom to the radius of the nucleus.
worked_example.tip: Equivalent ratios such as 1 × 10⁵ : 1 are accepted. The correct answer with no working scores full marks.

worked_example.question:
A typical atom has a radius of 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁰ m.

A molecule consists of 20 of these atoms in a long line.

Calculate the length of this molecule.

Write your answer in standard form.
worked_example.tip: The 2 turns the radius into a diameter. The correct answer on the answer line scores both marks.
